extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, law students, and legal practitioners dealing with patent assignments and title issues
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards governing patent assignments: what an assignment must contain and how it is construed, recording and notice rules, warranties (title and validity), reformation, and the validity/enforceability of contracts obligating assignment of future inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special tenures and conditional assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles conveyed by assignments are usually unconditional, but they may also be held upon special tenures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A condition establishing the special tenure should be stated in the assignment; the tenure may be expressed and the condition defined in a separate unrecorded paper with equal effect between the parties, but not effective against purchasers from the assignee who had no notice of the special tenure. The burden of proving non-compliance rests on the party who asserts it; where non-compliance is proved and no intervening rights exist, title reverts to the assignor by operation of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from denying filled blank assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who issue signed assignments in blank, are estopped from denying the propriety of the filling, when the filled assignments are invoked by purchasers for valuable considerations, who had no notice of any fraud or error in the filling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchasers for value without notice who rely on filled-in blank assignments are protected; the issuer cannot later deny the filling's propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent description requirements in assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent assigned ought to be described in the assignment by its number and date, and by the name of the patentee, and by the name of the invention which it purports to cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment will be valid though lacking or erroneous in one or more particulars if the description contained excludes doubt as to the patent intended (e.g., a broad clause conveying 'all the property ... including ... patents'). An assignment of a machine will not convey any process patent merely because the machine is used in that process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and authentication of assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment by a natural person requires no other authentication than the assignor's signature; where executed by an attorney in fact it must be executed in the name of the assignor and not in the attorney's own name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a power of attorney requires approval of assignments by the giver, an assignment made without such approval is void. A certificate of acknowledgment (notary) is prima facie evidence of genuineness and execution. The designation of the assignee is sufficient where the person intended can be identified, even if outside evidence is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments to partnerships and corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be assigned to a partnership by the partnership name; an assignment by a corporation need not be authenticated by its corporate seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment is properly executed if made in the name and by the authority of the corporation by a proper officer who signs as such. An assignment to a corporation confers no title on individual stockholders; an assignment to a corporation not yet organized will, by estoppel, inure to its benefit when organized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of special persons as assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: A married woman, an infant, or a person under guardianship may be the assignee of an invention or of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such persons must comply not only with U.S. law requiring written assignments but also with the particular State laws that govern analogous acts for other personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration/payment and effect on title
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment in which the consideration was never paid, and which was never acted upon by either of the parties thereto, conveys no title to the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignment has been acted upon by the parties, it cannot be revoked for partial failure to pay; total failure to pay does not derogate the rights of those who take title under it without notice. Where no third-party rights have accrued, an assignee may restore title to the assignor by destroying the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad contracts obligating assignment of future inventions — general invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contract which broadly obligates an inventor to assign without further consideration than the mere payment of money or transfer of property to the inventor all inventions which he may make during his lifetime is invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such contracts are treated under common-law restraint-of-trade principles and equitable unconscionability; overly broad grant-to-assign-all-future-inventions is generally void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts assigning future inventions valid when protecting business (reasonableness test)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the purpose intended and effected by the contract is the protection of the other's business from advantages that have or may be gained by the inventor from his relations with the other, the contract is not void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recent cases test validity not by inflexible rules but by reasonableness in connection with the protection necessary for the particular business and modern methods of conducting the enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment contracts assigning inventions relating to specified articles
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract of employment providing that the employee shall assign to the employer all inventions made during employment which relate to specified articles manufactured by the employer is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an invention relates both to specified and other articles, the contract will be enforced only to the extent it concerns the specified articles. A contract to assign inventions to a corporation formed for carrying on a related business is valid and specifically enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of future improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment of a patent by an agreement which provides for the assignment of all future improvements thereon to be made by the patentee is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conveying future improvements may be proper to protect the value of a basic patent; courts have upheld such clauses as reasonable to prevent hostile competition and preserve the basic patent's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of action for past infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights of action for past infringements of a patent are not conveyed by any mere assignment of that patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such rights may be conveyed if the assignment document expressly purports to convey them, either along with the patent or alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of assignments and parol evidence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction of assignments depends primarily upon the meaning of all the language in which they are composed; if that language is clear in the eye of the law, its effect cannot be varied by any parol evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the language is ambiguous, parol evidence is admissible to show collateral documents, surrounding circumstances, or that both parties thereafter practically construed the assignment alike. Parties cannot testify solely to their subjective prior intentions. Remaining ambiguities are solved against the grantor in suits between grantor and grantee, but as between grantee (or privies) and strangers, ambiguities are solved against the grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reformation of assignments in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformation of an assignment may be had by bill in equity if the assignment does not conform to the mutual intention of the parties to its execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reformation cannot be granted on proof of one party's intention alone; both parties' mutual intention must be shown. Reformation cannot affect the rights of any innocent purchaser for valuable consideration who had no notice at time of purchase. An assignee omitted a patent by mistake has an equitable right to have the assignment reformed to include it; that equitable right is transferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extensions and meaning of 'renewal'
rubrics_metrics.description: No extension of a patent is conveyed by an assignment of the first term thereof; the word 'renewal' in such an assignment is held to mean 'reissue' and not 'extension' unless the statutes at the time provide for extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment of an invention without limitation will convey the original term and any Patent Office extension; whether it conveys a Congressional extension is undecided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording in Patent Office and constructive notice (three-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording in the Patent Office, within three months after its date, is necessary to the validity of an assignment or grant of a patent as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for valuable consideration without notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording operates to give constructive notice to subsequent purchasers and mortgagees. The rule does not apply to assignments executed prior to grant unless the assignment is one upon which a patent is to be issued to the assignee and identifies the invention with certainty. Instruments not purporting to convey existing interests are not covered. Recording also does not apply to bankrupt trustees by operation of bankruptcy law. Recording is unnecessary as between the parties to the assignment and not necessary against an infringer; for accrued rights only, the assignee should give notice to the infringer to protect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of notice and what constitutes constructive notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice which will protect a prior unrecorded assignment may be actual, or it may be constructive only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive notice may be based on any fact within the knowledge or means of knowledge of the purchaser that should logically lead him, upon inquiry, to discover the assignment's existence and purport (e.g., statements in chain of title, or that the prior assignee was making, using, or selling specimens of the invention). Such making/using/selling charges cognizant purchasers with notice. Whether a subsequent purchaser being a corporation in which the assignor is a director constitutes constructive notice is disputed. Once title vests in a subsequent purchaser for value without notice, that title becomes absolute and may be purchased by persons with actual knowledge of the prior assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of assignment and three-month period
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of an assignment is the day of its delivery, not the date on its face if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three months within which recording is required are calendar months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied warranty of title in assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Warranty of title is implied in every assignment of a patent right unless the assignment purports to convey merely the right of the assignor or is otherwise limited more narrowly than the entire patent right described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an assignment will transfer whatever title the assignor may subsequently acquire. An assignment of 'the right, title and interest of the assignor' without more will not operate to convey title subsequently acquired by him.

rubrics_metrics.name: No implied warranty of validity; fraud exception
rubrics_metrics.description: No warranty of validity is implied in any assignment of a patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignor knows the patent to be invalid when making the assignment he is guilty of fraud and the assignee may have relief; if both parties are equally innocent, the loss falls on the owner of the patent. An assignee generally may not defend against a suit for the purchase price by claiming patent invalidity; an assignment of an invalid patent is nevertheless sufficient consideration to support a promissory note where there is neither warranty nor fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express and parol warranties of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Express warranties of validity may be incorporated in assignments and will subject assignors to actions for damages if patents are found invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parol warranties of validity accompanying written assignments are inadmissible as foundations for damages actions based solely on alleged invalidity, but such parol statements may be admissible to help prove fraud when other evidence shows the assignor knew of invalidity; the assignee's remedy in that case rests on fraud rather than the parol warranty.
